### A new look: the matte

The interface is the board a picture is mounted on, so it has stopped competing with the
wallpapers. The chrome is achromatic — a true-neutral graphite, no violet cast in the darks — and
the only colour in the window now comes from the wallpapers themselves. Selection and the primary
action are paper white rather than a brand hue.

- Glass panels, blur and the shadow under every box are gone. Depth comes from one value step and
  a hairline, which is what tells you a surface is raised.
- Corners are nearly flat, and tighter on images than on controls: a picture should not have its
  corners cropped by the frame around it.
- Cards sit still. The lift-and-zoom on hover cropped the picture you were trying to judge.
- Filters are squared switches, filled when on, instead of pills tinted to suggest it.
- The active page is a white rule in the margin rather than a coloured pill.
- Pages no longer slide up when you open them. Motion answers what you do; it does not perform on
  arrival.
- A narrow window collapses the sidebar to icons and gives the room to the wallpapers.

The typefaces stay the ones your system already uses — Lumen should look like it belongs on your
desktop, and bundling a webfont would cost download size and break offline.

### Also fixed

The window controls no longer take the whole interface down when Lumen's frontend is opened
outside the app, which is how this design was reviewed.

### Which file do I download?

| System | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 | `Lumen_4.2.3_x64-setup.exe` (or `..._portable.exe`, no installer) |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `Lumen_4.2.3_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `Lumen_4.2.3_x64.dmg` |
| Debian / Ubuntu / Mint | `Lumen_4.2.3_amd64.deb` |
| Fedora / openSUSE | `Lumen-4.2.3-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Any other Linux | `Lumen_4.2.3_amd64.AppImage` |

On Windows, 4.2.2 installs this one itself.
